sections.content:
47,550 people

were counted on the census as "engineering technicians" in England and Wales in March 2021.

Engineering technicians perform a variety of technical support functions to assist engineers with the design, development, operation, installation and maintenance of engineering systems and constructions.

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "engineering technicians" there were more men than women (90.8% compared with 9.2%).

This means "engineering technicians" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "science, engineering and technology associate professionals".

Men made up 90.8% and women made up 9.2% of "engineering technicians"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "engineering technicians" included:

  • precision instrument makers and repairers
  • metal making and treating process operatives
  • train and tram drivers

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

People who had this job were generally similar in age to the working population

The occupation of "engineering technicians" had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 25 to 29 years. Of the whole working population 11.1% were aged 25 to 29 years. For people working as "engineering technicians", 14% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "engineering technicians" was 65 years or older.

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "engineering technicians" included:

  • delivery operatives
  • electrical and electronics technicians
  • collector salespersons and credit agents

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

We can look at who worked as "engineering technicians" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Among those aged 50 years and older, we see there is a higher proportion of men with this occupation than women.

The percentage of men and women who are "engineering technicians" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "engineering technicians", 7% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (93.2% compared with 6.8%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (92.9%) than self-employed (7.1%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Birmingham, this is in the region of the West Midlands.
